topic.title: Delta's 2025 pre-tax profit next to what American Express paid it for miles and the co-brand card

title: The airline's quiet partner is in your wallet ✈️
description:
Does Delta only make its money flying you?
Of Delta's 2025 revenue, a credit card company paid more than the airline's whole pre-tax profit. Figures from Delta's 2025 results (SEC filing).
Speak to a licensed financial adviser in your country before acting on money decisions.
An animated story with illustrative numbers; the characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Did your card just pay for a plane? Comment

lines.text: Delta makes its money flying you? Watch this.
Last year, Delta took in $63.4B in revenue.
But after costs, only $6.2B was left before tax.
And who else pays Delta, besides flyers?
Of its revenue, American Express alone paid $8.2B.
That's more than Delta's whole profit before tax.
Your card buys Delta's miles. Is it only the seats?

Facts confirmed on the SEC 8-K page (13 Jan 2026): GAAP pre-tax income $6.2B (9.8% margin), operating revenue $63.4B, Amex remuneration $8.2B (up 11%). The figures are fine; the framing fails.

Title 'Airlines don't make their money on your seat' (and thumbnail 'Not your seat', payoff 'Still think it's the seats?', hook cross 'Not quite'): says seats are not where airlines make their money. That breaks the topic's verify rule (never say airlines make 'most' of their money from cards). Passenger fares are still most of Delta's $63.4B, and the video talks about one airline but the title says 'Airlines'. Reword, e.g. 'A credit card paid Delta more than its whole profit' and 'Is it only the seats?'.

Beats ask/amex/turn ('So where does the real money come from?' -> Amex $8.2B -> 'That's more than Delta's whole profit before tax'): presents the $8.2B as new money outside the $63.4B, and as if it were the profit. It is revenue that is already inside the $63.4B, and it has costs (the miles Delta has to honour). The verify list says never call it pure profit. Keep the comparison but say it is already part of the revenue and is not all profit (e.g. 'Of that $63.4B, American Express alone paid $8.2B, more than Delta's whole pre-tax profit'), and drop 'real money'.

Description: 'illustrative numbers' is wrong, since the figures are real and sourced (say 'figures from Delta's 2025 results'). The profile's 'speak to a licensed financial adviser in your country' line is also missing; add it before the disclaimer.
